newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Gunfire breaks out in Cambodia capital.
newsitem.headline: Gunfire breaks out in Cambodia capital.

text.p: Phnom Penh, June 17 (Reuter ) - Heavy firing broke out in the capital of Cambodia just before midnight on Tuesday, witnesses said.
They reported heavy firing from automatic weapons, grenades and mortar or tanks near the centre of the city. But the cause of the firing was not immediately clear in the darkened streets of the city.
Reuters photographer Patrick de Noirmont, who was in Norodom Avenue, a main thoroughfare, said streets were virtually empty as residents took cover in their homes to avoid the gunfire.
Some residents said the intense firing, which went on for almost 45 minutes, appeared to be coming from near the home of co-premier Norodom Ranariddh. But that could not be confirmed.

The shooting fell away in intensity after about an hour, but it was not immediately clear if the fighting had ended. Police sirens wailed through the city and police were setting up roadblocks, de Noirmont reported.

The fighting came as Pol Pot, mastermind of the 1975-79 Khmer Rouge "killing fields" rule of Cambodia, was reported to be on the run toward Thailand with a handful of followers, holding several senior guerrillas, following thousands of defections in the reviled Maoist faction over the past 10 months.
